prototype.headline: No OAuth app needed to start: connect through Composio's managed Linear app.

production.headline: Linear OAuth can be set up quickly, but review or paid‑plan requirements are uncertain.

verdict.confidence: high on OAuth support, token lifetimes and rate‑limit details; uncertain about any hidden app‑review or paid‑plan requirements
verdict.summary: Linear offers a fully self‑serve OAuth2 flow. You can create an app, configure redirects, and start making API calls without a provider review. Operational limits are request quotas (5 000 req/h per OAuth app) and optional client‑credentials token caps.

stages.name: Connect through Composio's managed Linear app

steps.text: Create a Composio session for your user. Do not pass an auth config for linear, so the managed app is used.
Send the user a Connect Link. They approve on Linear's consent screen, which shows Composio's app name.
Run one test tool call to confirm the connection works.

stages.name: Determine whether the managed Linear integration meets your needs

steps.text: If the default Composio managed Linear OAuth integration provides the scopes and quota you need, you can skip the remaining stages.
Otherwise, proceed to create your own Linear OAuth application.
In a Linear workspace where you are an admin, go to **Settings → API** and click **Create a new OAuth2 Application**.
Enter a name and description (shown on the consent screen) and save the app.
Add the exact redirect URI(s) your integration will use. Linear accepts any HTTPS URL and also localhost URLs (e.g., http://localhost:3000/oauth/callback).

stages.name: Select grant type and optional PKCE

steps.text: For typical user‑auth flows keep the default **authorization_code** grant. Enable **PKCE** if you prefer a secret‑less flow.
If you need server‑to‑server access, enable **client_credentials** tokens (requires toggling the option in the app settings).
Generate an authorization URL for the newly created app, complete the login flow, and capture the authorization code.
Exchange the code for an access token (valid for 24 hours) and a refresh token.
Call the Linear GraphQL endpoint (`https://api.linear.app/graphql`) with the access token and verify a successful response.
Toggle **client credentials tokens** in the app settings, then request a token via `POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token` with `grant_type=client_credentials`.
Remember the token is valid for 30 days and you can have up to 1 000 active client‑credentials tokens in parallel.

stages.name: Review rate limits and plan for scaling

steps.text: OAuth apps are limited to 5 000 requests per hour per user. If you need higher limits, contact Linear support to request an increase.
Paid workspaces may receive dynamic higher limits based on the number of paid users.

requirements: Admin access to a Linear workspace to create an OAuth app
HTTPS redirect URI (or localhost for development)
Client ID and client secret from the Linear app settings
If using PKCE, a code verifier/challenge pair
If using client‑credentials, enable the option in the app settings
If you want Linear's MCP server rather than its API, that is a separate Composio toolkit (LINEAR_MCP) with its own auth (k5).

blockers.issue: If you need more than 5 000 requests per hour, Linear may deny higher quota without a paid plan.
blockers.whenItHits: When your integration approaches the hourly limit
blockers.whatToDo: Open a support ticket with Linear to request a higher quota; consider using a paid workspace for dynamic limits.

blockers.issue: Client‑credentials token limit of 1 000 active tokens may be hit in large‑scale server‑to‑server deployments.
blockers.whenItHits: When you generate many parallel tokens
blockers.whatToDo: Reuse a single token per deployment or rotate tokens less frequently; ensure you stay within the 1 000 token cap.

agentCanDo: Generate a Connect Link for the Linear OAuth app
Poll the connection status until the user authorizes the app
Exchange authorization codes for access and refresh tokens
Perform sample GraphQL API calls with the obtained token
youMustDo: Log into a Linear workspace as an admin and create the OAuth app
Configure redirect URIs and enable optional features (PKCE, client‑credentials)
Store the client secret securely and rotate it if compromised
Request higher rate limits or quota increases from Linear support if needed

claims.text: Linear supports OAuth2 authentication for building integrations.
Linear supports the PKCE flow for OAuth2.
Access tokens issued by Linear are valid for 24 hours.
Linear returns a refresh token that can be used to obtain new access tokens.
Linear supports the client_credentials grant; tokens are valid for 30 days and up to 1 000 active tokens are allowed per app.
OAuth apps are limited to 5 000 requests per hour per user.
Linear applies dynamic rate limits for workspace‑level OAuth apps based on the number of paid users.
Redirect URIs may be any HTTPS URL or a localhost URL (e.g., http://localhost:3000/oauth/callback).
Linear does not advertise a Dynamic Client Registration endpoint.

composioTail: In the Composio dashboard go to Auth Configs, click Create Auth Config, select the toolkit and choose OAuth2.
Copy the redirect URI shown in the Composio dashboard and register it in the provider's app settings.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the provider app overview into the Composio auth config, and click Create.
Copy the resulting auth config ID (looks like ac_xxxx). Keep secrets out of source control.
Pass the auth config ID to your session: authConfigs: { [toolkit]: 'ac_xxxx' }. Toolkits not listed keep using Composio managed auth.
